fixtureDivergences.note: Render-conformance section: the shared conformance corpus (packages/adapter-tests) is rendered through every adapter’s REAL backend and byte-compared against the Hono reference. This answers, per fixture and per adapter, whether the construct WORKS — not just whether it compiles. A construct works either as written (✓) or with a documented `/* @client */` comment (✓†, a verified, supported escape — most refusals have one). Fixtures absent from the table below work on every adapter — most as written, some via that documented escape; the headline says how many of each. Listed fixtures need attention somewhere: a bare diagnostic code is still-open debt with no escape yet, a code led by ✗ owes no escape at all (by design), and ≠ means the fixture compiles clean but its rendered output diverges from the reference.

escape.reason: By design: this fixture is the SSR-adopting-hydration + patch-on-update regression pin for #2389. A '/* @client */' escape twin would SSR an empty region, eliminating the adopted DOM node the fixture exists to test patching — collapsing it to the already-covered client-only-loop case with zero new coverage. It is also deliberately kept out of integrations/shared/components (per this file's own docstring) because every DSL integration app's bf build compiles that directory wholesale, so no DSL escape variant is wanted there either.

ambient-locale-date-formatting.title: Ambient-locale Date formatting
ambient-locale-date-formatting.given: a `Date`-typed prop formatted with zero-argument `toLocaleDateString()` (no explicit locale or options)
ambient-locale-date-formatting.expected: the date renders formatted for the server process default locale
ambient-locale-date-formatting.actual: the compiler refuses with BF021 (by design)
ambient-locale-date-formatting.reason: The zero-argument form resolves against the runtime environment ambient locale (ICU/CLDR data, `LC_*`), which is not knowable at build time and differs across every backend language and between the server and the browser. Any lowering would be a silent SSR/CSR divergence; a Hono carve-out was tried and rejected because hydration re-evaluates the expression against a JSON-de-riched receiver. The literal-locale and named-timezone forms are lowered instead.

computed-const-loop-source.expected: the rows render in the server HTML

data-on-attr-value-script-escaped.title: A dynamic value on a `data-on…` attribute renders as a quoted script string
data-on-attr-value-script-escaped.given: an element attribute named `data-` followed by a name starting with `on` (`data-on`, `data-onset`) whose value is dynamic (`<div data-on={mode()}>`)
data-on-attr-value-script-escaped.expected: the attribute carries the value as plain text (`data-on="x"`), like any other `data-*` attribute
data-on-attr-value-script-escaped.actual: renders the value as a script string literal, so the attribute text carries escaped double quotes around it (`"x"` instead of `x`, `""` for an empty value), because the template engine escapes a `data-on…` attribute as an event-handler attribute

derived-object-literal-signal.title: Derived object-literal signal initializer
derived-object-literal-signal.given: a `createSignal` / `createMemo` whose initial value is an object literal referencing a live prop (with or without a spread)
derived-object-literal-signal.expected: field reads on the signal render the values the caller passed

fragment-wrapped-conditional-return-bran.title: Fragment-wrapped branch of a conditional return is never hydrated
fragment-wrapped-conditional-return-bran.given: a component with an early-return branch whose other branch is wrapped in a fragment (`if (x) return <a/>; return <><button/></>`)
fragment-wrapped-conditional-return-bran.expected: the rendered branch root carries the component scope id on every render path, so its events bind

jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.title: JSX wrapped in a ternary or array at a non-children prop
jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.given: a component prop other than `children` whose value is a ternary or array literal wrapping JSX elements (`header={cond ? <a/> : <b/>}`)
jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.expected: the chosen elements render inside the child in the server HTML
jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.actual: the compiler refuses with BF021 (by design)
jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.reason: The shape is refused in the shared JSX-to-IR phase, identically on every adapter including the reference: the classifier has no structured node for it, and the only alternative was splicing raw JSX source text into the emitted client JS untyped. Passing the elements as `children`, or lifting the ternary into a single JSX element, is the supported form.

line-statement-sigil-text-after-conditio.title: Text starting with a colon or percent sign right after a ternary
line-statement-sigil-text-after-conditio.given: static JSX text whose first non-space character is `:` or `%`, directly following a ternary conditional whose branches both render (`{c ? 'on' : 'off'} :y`, `{c ? 'on' : 'off'} %y`)
line-statement-sigil-text-after-conditio.expected: the text renders verbatim after the chosen branch (`off :y`)
line-statement-sigil-text-after-conditio.actual: throws a template parse error because the engine reads the text as a statement line, or drops the text when that line happens to parse

literal-const-conditional-test.title: Literal-initialized const read as a conditional test
literal-const-conditional-test.given: a `const` initialized with a boolean literal at module or function scope (`const on = true`), or with a string literal inside the component function (`const mode = 'on'`), read as the test of a ternary (`data-x={on ? 'a' : 'b'}`, `data-x={mode === 'on' ? 'a' : 'b'}`)
literal-const-conditional-test.expected: the branch the const's value selects renders in the server HTML (`data-x="a"`)
literal-const-conditional-test.actual: renders the falsy branch as if the const were unset, or throws at render time on an unbound template variable

loop-component-row-destructured-param.title: A component loop row loses its row values when the callback destructures the row param
loop-component-row-destructured-param.given: a `.map()` loop over a memo whose callback destructures its row param and whose row body is a component keyed by a destructured field, receiving a destructured field as a prop on itself or on a component in its forwarded children (`shown().map(({ id, tone }) => <Mark key={id} tone={tone} />)`, `shown().map(({ id, tone }) => <Chip key={id}><Mark tone={tone} /></Chip>)`)
loop-component-row-destructured-param.expected: one component per row, each with its own key and prop (`data-key="a" data-tone="warm"`, `data-key="b" data-tone="cool"`), hydrated with the same values
loop-component-row-destructured-param.actual: renders no rows at all, or rows without their `data-key` and without the destructured prop; and the emitted client JS reads the destructured name where it is not bound (`get tone() { return tone }`), so hydrating or creating a row throws a `ReferenceError`

loop-row-child-children-attrs-frozen.title: A loop-row child component's forwarded JSX children can't reach an outer signal/memo at SSR
loop-row-child-children-attrs-frozen.given: a static `.map()` loop row that calls a child component passing a JSX element as `children`, where that element reads an OUTER signal/memo — not just the row's own item (e.g. `…` inside `items.map(item => …)`, module- or function-scope array alike)
loop-row-child-children-attrs-frozen.expected: the row's markup — including the forwarded child element, evaluated against the signal's initial value — renders at SSR the same way a non-loop reference to the same signal does

loop-row-child-children-prop-array.title: Component loop row with forwarded children over an array prop
loop-row-child-children-prop-array.given: a `.map()` over an array prop of objects whose row is a child component receiving forwarded JSX children that read the row (`props.items.map(item => <Badge key={item.id}>{item.label}</Badge>)`)
loop-row-child-children-prop-array.expected: one component per row, each with its own key and forwarded children (`data-key="a"` … `A`, `data-key="b"` … `B`)
loop-row-child-children-prop-array.actual: renders the loop empty with no diagnostic: the props constructor builds no rows from the array prop (nor from the child's own input rows), and a row slice filled in after construction fails at render time because the row wrapper has no field for the row data the forwarded children read (`can't evaluate field Label`)

loop-row-child-key-not-a-prop.title: Component loop row keyed by a row field the component takes no prop for
loop-row-child-key-not-a-prop.given: a `.map()` over an array prop of objects whose row is a child component with no children, keyed by a field of the row object the component has no same-named prop for (`props.items.map(item => <Badge key={item.id} label={item.label} />)`, where `Badge` takes only `label`)
loop-row-child-key-not-a-prop.expected: one component per row, each with its own key and prop (`data-key="a"` … `A`, `data-key="b"` … `B`)
loop-row-child-key-not-a-prop.actual: emits code that fails to build: it reads the key field off the child component's input struct, which has no such field (`BadgeInput has no field or method ID`)

loop-row-child-key-shadowed-by-prop.title: Component loop row keyed by a row field the component also takes a same-named prop for
loop-row-child-key-shadowed-by-prop.given: a `.map()` over an array prop of objects whose row is a child component with no children, keyed by a field of the row object whose name the component also takes as a prop, passed a different row field (`props.items.map(item => <Badge key={item.id} id={item.slug} label={item.label} />)`)
loop-row-child-key-shadowed-by-prop.expected: one component per row, each keyed by the row field and given the prop (`data-id="x" data-key="a"` … `A`, `data-id="y" data-key="b"` … `B`)
loop-row-child-key-shadowed-by-prop.actual: renders each row's `data-key` from the child's same-named prop instead of the row field (`data-key="x"`, `data-key="y"`): the props constructor reads the key off each row's child-component input

loop-row-child-nested-prop-reads-unreach.title: A component in a loop-row child's forwarded children loses a prop read from the row index or a callback-body local
loop-row-child-nested-prop-reads-unreach.given: a `.map()` loop whose row is a single child component with forwarded JSX `children`, where those children nest another component whose prop reads a callback binding other than the row item itself: the index parameter (`opts.map((o, i) => <Chip><Mark pos={i}>…</Mark></Chip>)`) or a local the callback body declares (`const t = o.tone` → `<Mark tone={t}>`)
loop-row-child-nested-prop-reads-unreach.expected: each row renders the nested component with its own value (`data-pos="0"`, `data-pos="1"`; `data-tone="warm"`, `data-tone="cool"`)
loop-row-child-nested-prop-reads-unreach.actual: renders every row's nested component with the prop's zero value instead (the attribute is missing), because the forwarded children render as a separate template that receives the row item but not the row's other bindings

loop-row-child-scalar-row-key.title: Component loop row keyed by the row value of a scalar array prop
loop-row-child-scalar-row-key.given: a `.map()` over an array prop of strings whose row is a child component with no children, keyed by the row value itself rather than a field of it (`props.items.map(i => <Badge key={i} label={i} />)`)
loop-row-child-scalar-row-key.expected: one component per row, each with its own key and prop (`data-key="a"` … `a`, `data-key="b"` … `b`)
loop-row-child-scalar-row-key.actual: renders every row without its `data-key`: the props constructor only takes a row key from a field of each row's child-component input, and the row value itself is not one

loop-row-ref-portal.title: A `ref`-callback portal on a loop-row element
loop-row-ref-portal.given: an element inside a keyed `.map()` row that has an event handler and a `ref` callback moving it out of the row with `createPortal(el, document.body, { ownerScope })`
loop-row-ref-portal.expected: the server HTML and the hydrated DOM agree, and clicking the element runs its handler
loop-row-ref-portal.actual: renders the element inside its row and moves it to `document.body` at hydration (a callback declared in the row callback places it at the portal outlet already in the server HTML), after which clicking it no longer runs its handler

module-scope-helper-call.title: Module-scope helper called from a template position
module-scope-helper-call.given: a template expression calling a module-scope helper by bare name (an arrow-valued `const`, a `function` declaration, or a chain of them), in text or boolean-test position
module-scope-helper-call.expected: the helper runs at render time and its result renders in the server HTML
module-scope-helper-call.actual: the compiler refuses with BF101 / BF102

namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.title: Reactive primitive called through a namespace import
namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.given: a reactive primitive invoked through a namespace import (`import * as bf`, `bf.createSignal(...)`) in a compile with no shared `ts.Program`
namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.expected: the signal is declared and the component hydrates
namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.actual: the compiler refuses with BF013 (by design)
namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.reason: Without a type checker the analyzer fast path matches only a bare identifier callee, so the declaration would be silently dropped and every reference would throw at hydrate. The loud refusal is the permanent answer for checker-less compiles; a compile that supplies a shared program (the Vite plugin does) resolves the primitive normally and never reaches it. Importing the primitive by name is the supported form.

nested-callback-in-filter-predicate.title: Nested higher-order callback inside a filter predicate
nested-callback-in-filter-predicate.given: a `.filter()` predicate whose body calls `.some()` / `.find()` with its own arrow callback
nested-callback-in-filter-predicate.expected: the filtered rows render in the server HTML with the nested predicate applied

nested-prop-member-signal-seed.title: Signal seeded from a member of an object-typed prop
nested-prop-member-signal-seed.given: a `createSignal` whose initial value is a member of an object-typed prop (`createSignal(initial.label)`, `createSignal(initial.items)`), read by the component as text, a conditional, or a loop source, or forwarded to a child component prop
nested-prop-member-signal-seed.expected: the server HTML renders the seeded value, as if the member had been passed as a top-level prop

off-subset-callback-body.title: Off-subset expression in a collection-method callback
off-subset-callback-body.expected: the callback runs and the result renders in the server HTML
off-subset-callback-body.actual: the compiler refuses with BF021 / BF101

opaque-local-accessor-call.title: Opaque local accessor invoked from a template position
opaque-local-accessor-call.given: a component-body `const` bound to the result of a call the compiler cannot evaluate (a helper returning a function, or an accessor returned by a library), invoked with `()` in text position
opaque-local-accessor-call.expected: the accessor runs at render time and its result renders in the server HTML

ref-effect-attr-state-ssr.title: Attribute written only by a ref callback never reaches SSR
ref-effect-attr-state-ssr.given: an element whose `ref` callback unconditionally writes an attribute on mount — `el.setAttribute('<name>', …)` or `el.dataset.<key> = …`, at the top level of the ref body or of a `createEffect` / `onMount` directly inside it — that the element's own JSX never renders
ref-effect-attr-state-ssr.expected: the server HTML and the hydrated DOM carry the same attribute value

rich-typed-prop-hydration.title: Rich-typed prop read by client code
rich-typed-prop-hydration.given: a prop typed as a JSON-unsafe host type (`Map`, `Set`, `WeakMap`, `WeakSet`, `URLSearchParams`, `RegExp`, `Promise`, `Error`, `Symbol`, `BigInt`, `Function`) that the component own client code reads
rich-typed-prop-hydration.expected: the client handler sees the same value the server rendered with
rich-typed-prop-hydration.actual: the compiler refuses with BF049 (by design)
rich-typed-prop-hydration.reason: Props cross the `bf-p` hydration boundary as `JSON.stringify` data with no type-aware revival, so these types lose their contents (`Map` / `Set` serialize to `{}`, `BigInt` throws, `Promise` / `Function` cannot cross a serialization boundary at all). A typed revival envelope was considered and rejected as a nine-adapter protocol change that still could not carry every listed type. The sound path is to pass a JSON-safe value and rebuild the rich value client-side.

signal-read-in-nested-static-loop.title: Signal read inside a nested static loop row
signal-read-in-nested-static-loop.given: a static (non-signal) array `.map()` whose row contains a nested `.map()` reading a signal or memo getter
signal-read-in-nested-static-loop.expected: both loop levels render in the server HTML with the signal initial value

statement-body-callback.title: Statement-carrying .map() / .flatMap() callback body
statement-body-callback.given: a `.map()` or `.flatMap()` callback whose body is a block with statements (an imperative array builder, a const preamble feeding a leaf, an early return)
statement-body-callback.expected: the callback body runs and every row renders in the server HTML

static-literal-loop-component-row.title: Child component in a row of a loop over a static literal array
static-literal-loop-component-row.given: a `.map()` over a module- or function-scope `const` initialized with a static array literal, whose row renders a child component anywhere other than as the row root (inside an element, a conditional branch or a nested loop)
static-literal-loop-component-row.expected: every row renders in the server HTML

text-adjacent-conditional-whitespace.title: Whitespace between static text and an adjacent conditional
text-adjacent-conditional-whitespace.given: static JSX text directly adjacent to a conditional expression with no whitespace between them, before it (`x:{c ? 'on' : 'off'}`) or after it (`{c ? 'on' : 'off'}:y`), whether the condition reads a signal or a prop
text-adjacent-conditional-whitespace.expected: the text and the chosen branch abut with no whitespace between them (`x:off`, `off:y`)
text-adjacent-conditional-whitespace.actual: renders a space between the text and the chosen branch (`x: off`, `off :y`)

untyped-loop-array-no-row-struct.title: Untyped object-literal loop array with no single row shape
untyped-loop-array-no-row-struct.given: a `.map()` whose rows call a child component, over an unannotated module-scope `const` array of object literals whose rows do not share one set of fields with one plain type each: for example the rows have different keys, or a field is a nested object, a `null`, a non-identifier key, an empty nested array, or a value whose type differs between rows
untyped-loop-array-no-row-struct.expected: the rows render in the server HTML
